learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.exploration: Default 6 hours was low tide. Moon-facing preset at zero was high; opposite at 12 h 25 min high; quarter turn at 6 h 12 min low. Slider End at 24 h 48 min returned high.
observations.reveal: Corrected to two, described two bulges and coast crossing both, 12 h 25 min spacing and 24 h 50 min lunar day. Explained near water pulled harder than centre and far water less, so differential attraction stretches ocean.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Two exaggerated blue bulges, coast dot, Moon and three differently sized same-direction arrows visible. Toy no-continents caveat and lunar-day definition legible. Slider endpoint showed 24 h 48 while prose used 24 h 50.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Simple count targets one Moon one tide intuition.
prediction.evidence: One selected against two and four.

interaction.reason: Three orientations and full-day boundary distinguish both high states and low state.
interaction.evidence: Zero and opposite high; quarter low; endpoint high.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains far-side bulge through differential pull.
payoff.evidence: Near, centre and far attraction ordering.

clarity.reason: Dot and force arrows support explanation with explicit toy limits.
clarity.evidence: No continents, exaggerated bulges and lunar-day definition shown.

transfer.reason: Differential-force principle stays in the same tidal example.
transfer.evidence: No new application or coast-specific case tested.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard endpoint and tide text worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: High tide also occurs facing away from Moon.

visualExplanation.reason: Two bulges and unequal pull arrows explain spatial pattern.

playfulness.reason: Rotation control moves a coast through the cycle.

practicalValue.reason: Explains common tide count in ideal model.
practicalValue.evidence: Most-coasts qualifier but no local prediction.

depth.evidence: Centre pulls away from far-side water relative to near side.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Compare attraction across Earth and relate fixed bulges to rotating coastline.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Lunar day and tidal differential introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Hours and minutes, high/low labels and arrow lengths.

whyCool: The far-side high tide becomes understandable when pull is compared across Earth.
caveat: No continents model cannot predict a specific coast; displayed endpoint 24 h 48 differs slightly from explanatory 24 h 50.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
